transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because things got scary at work. I’m a waitress, and during service I started freezing up, like just stopping in the middle of what I was doing. Sometimes I’d do things completely out of order, like stand by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and just keep repeating table numbers instead of closing checks. It upset people, and honestly it scared me too.
Have you been having any recurring, intrusive thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get worried after things happen, and I’ll replay it a bit, but I don’t have one specific thought that keeps forcing its way in or anything like that.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors to relieve anxiety or stress?
No, not really. I don’t have rituals or things I feel like I have to do to make anxiety go away. I might get tense or confused, but I’m not doing specific routines on purpose like that.
Have you experienced any episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
I’m not sure I’d call them episodes like that. I do get scared when I freeze up or feel confused, but I haven’t noticed it coming on suddenly and peaking within a few minutes like a panic thing.
Did these episodes of freezing up and confusion at work seem to be triggered by something specific happening or was it more random?

It seemed more random to me. Like, it would happen right in the middle of service, not always because of one specific thing. I’d just freeze up or start doing things out of order—like standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing checks. That’s what scared everyone.
Have you experienced any traumatic events recently or in the past that might be connected to what's been happening at work?
I don’t think so. Nothing traumatic really comes to mind, either recently or from before, that I can connect to what’s been happening at work.
Have you been avoiding going to work or certain tasks at work since these episodes started happening?

I don’t really know. I haven’t been clearly avoiding work on purpose, but I do feel uneasy about it now. I still try to do what I’m supposed to, though I’m not sure if I’m steering away from certain tasks without realizing it.
Have your symptoms been affecting your relationships with coworkers or your overall ability to function at work?

Yes, it has. At work it’s gotten bad enough that I think I’m close to losing the shift-lead opportunity. My mistakes and the confusion have messed up service and closing more than once, and people notice.

And at home too… my husband says I’m barely present with him anymore. I don’t mean to be like that, but I guess I’m not really there the way I used to be.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships or daily activities outside of work due to how you've been feeling lately?

Yeah. I don’t really do the things I used to do much anymore. I used to go for walks on the beach, bake sometimes, work in the garden, write in my journal… but lately I just don’t get myself to start any of it.

And with my husband, when he tries to talk to me, I mostly just sit there. It’s not that I’m trying to ignore him. It just feels like I can’t really care or respond the way I should.
Do you think your symptoms at work are related to any particular stress or problem you're experiencing outside of work?

I’m not really sure. I can’t point to one specific problem outside of work that set it off. Things at home have been strained, but I don’t know if that’s causing the work stuff or if it’s just all mixed together.
Do you feel like your symptoms are significantly interfering with your ability to enjoy life or function normally?

Yes. I mean, it’s not just bothering me, it’s getting in the way of normal things. At work I’m making mistakes and getting confused enough that service and closing have been disrupted, and I’m worried I’m going to lose the shift-lead opportunity.

And at home, my husband says I’m barely present with him anymore. I don’t want that, but that’s how it’s been.
Do you ever feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body or like you're in a dream when these episodes happen?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed feeling like I’m outside my body or like I’m dreaming. It’s more that I get confused or kind of stuck, but not in that way.
Do you feel like you've been feeling less emotional or caring about things that normally would be important to you?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t really do the things I used to care about, like walking on the beach, baking, gardening, or writing in my journal. I just kind of stopped.

And when my husband tries to talk to me, I mostly just sit there. It’s not that I want to ignore him, it just feels like I can’t get myself to care or even start responding the way I should.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience emotions the way you used to?

Yeah… I think so. It’s like the feeling is dulled down. I don’t really get excited to do things I used to like, like beach walks or baking or gardening, and I barely write in my journal anymore.

And with my husband, when he tries to talk to me, I mostly just sit there. I know I should care and respond, but it feels like I can’t really start, or I can’t get myself to feel much.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy more than you feel like you're just not able to experience emotions about them?

I think it’s more like I’ve lost interest, but also I just can’t get myself to start anything. I don’t really go for beach walks or bake or garden anymore, and I hardly write in my journal.

Even when my husband tries to talk with me, I mostly just sit there. It feels like I can’t make myself care enough to respond.
How long have you been experiencing these episodes of freezing up and confusion at work?

It’s been happening for a little while now at work. I don’t know exactly when it started, but what scared people was me freezing up in the middle of service.

Like, I’d be standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and instead of closing checks I’d just keep repeating table numbers. Or I’d do things in the wrong order and get confused. It’s been enough that my coworkers noticed.
How many weeks or months have you been feeling this way, with the loss of interest and emotional dulling?

I’d say it’s been building for about a year and two months now. It started around when I was asked to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities, and since then I’ve just felt more and more… dulled down and not interested in things.
How many months have you been feeling this way, with the loss of interest and emotional dulling, without any significant improvement?
About fourteen months, I think. It’s been pretty much since I was asked to take on the evening shift lead duties, and it hasn’t really lifted since then.
Has your feeling of being dulled down and not interested in things lasted for more than two years?
No, not more than two years. It’s been about a year and two months, since I got asked to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities.
Have your symptoms of feeling dulled down and not interested in things lasted for more than two years now?
No, not more than two years. It’s been about a year and two months, since around when I was asked to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities.
